title: WPMS/972/2018 of Smt. Hemlata AND OTHERS Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPMS No.972 of 2018
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Mr. T.A. Khan, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. A.K.
Arya, Advocate for the petitioners.
 Mr. Yogesh Pandey, Additional C.S.C. with Mr. K.S.
Mehta, Brief Holder for the State/respondents.
Petitioners before this Court have filed the
present writ petition seeking the following relief(s):-
"(i). To issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondents to bring their case before the
respondent no. 5 for granting the petitioners an opportunity of
hearing as provided under UP Public Premises (Eviction of
Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1972 and the respondent no. 5 may
be directed to decide the case as provided under UP Public Premises
(Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1972.
(ii). To issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
"Prohibition" commanding the respondents not to take any action
against the petitioners with regard to the demolition of the buildings
of the petitioners situated at Village Jaspur Patti Tirmal, Jaspur Patti
Uttam, and Village Bhagwantpur, Tehsil Jaspur, District Udham
Singh Nagar, unless and until the matter is being decided by the
Prescribed Authority under the UP Public Premises (Eviction of
Unauthorized Occupants Act, 1972."
The petitioners apprehend that the construction
made by them is likely to be demolished as Prescribed
Authority/respondent no.5 has given notices to the
petitioners to demolish the encroachments made by the
petitioners on a public place.
Admittedly, the action of the Prescribed
Authority is in consequence of a general order passed
by the Division Bench of this Court in Writ Petition
(PIL) No. 128 of 2016. Moreover, the dispute before
this Court raises disputed questions of facts, which
cannot be appreciated in a writ petition. A writ petition
therefore is not a proper remedy in this case.
In view of the aforesaid, the writ petition stands
dismissed in limine.
 It is made clear that dismissal of the writ petition
would not prejudice the case of the petitioners to file a
civil suit, in case they are so advised.
 Let a certified copy of this order be issued today itself
on payment of usual charges.
